glance: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says weekend strikes on Bahrain targeted US Patriot sites; Gulf neighbors condemned the attack and new tanker incidents were reported Sunday.
Amazon is reportedly close to a $7.5 billion purchase of AI startup Decart, possibly announced next week.
Nvidia heads into a tense week: Washington wants board answers within 10 days, and chipmakers warn new US export rules reach further than expected.
The death toll from Russia's drone strike on an apartment block in Dymer near Kyiv has risen to four, with about 10 people still unaccounted for.
Bitcoin bounced about 5% to near $61,000 after Saturday's two-year low; stock futures reopen at 5 PM CT after Wall Street's worst week since April 2025.

tech.headline: Amazon reportedly nears $7.5 billion deal for AI startup Decart
tech.summary: Amazon is in advanced talks to buy Decart, which builds fast, efficient real-time AI generation models, in a deal worth about $7.5 billion that could come as soon as next week, the Financial Times reports. It would rank among Amazon's largest AI acquisitions and strengthen AWS's push to rival Nvidia in AI compute.

tech.headline: Nvidia faces a 10-day deadline from Washington amid SEC scrutiny
tech.summary: After reports that the SEC is examining Nvidia's accounting and disclosures, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he wants answers from the board and outside counsel within roughly 10 days. Nvidia has delayed its quarterly 10-Q and cited an independent board committee review. The stock lost nearly $900 billion in value last week, setting up a closely watched Monday open.

tech.headline: Chip-smuggling probe widens as China spy report lands
tech.summary: An FT investigation traces ties between businesswoman Alice Huang, gaming firms and shell companies allegedly used to move Nvidia chips into China. Separately, The New York Times reports China's Ministry of State Security has worked for at least two years to help Chinese firms obtain advanced AI chips; Beijing called the claims fabricated.

tech.headline: Supply chain warns new US export rules hit more than AI chips
tech.summary: Industry insiders told Nikkei Asia that the latest US export controls cover a broader range of semiconductors than expected, including system-on-chip parts used in consumer electronics. That could spread disruption well beyond data-center hardware into phones, PCs and other gadgets.

tech.headline: Bait test finds AI routers leaking users' secrets
tech.summary: Researchers fed planted fake credentials through AI routing services such as OpenRouter and Vercel and found privacy promises were often broken, even under zero-data-retention settings; some bait AWS keys were later tried tens of thousands of times by attackers. It is a strong reminder not to paste credentials into AI tools.

tech.headline: AI-aided proof tackles a famous Navier-Stokes problem
tech.summary: NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic's Levent Alpöge published an AI-assisted proof showing blowup in the Navier-Stokes fluid equations, Scientific American reports. If it holds up under expert review, it would be one of the most significant math results yet credited partly to AI.

tech.headline: Microsoft will retire its To Do app in June 2027
tech.summary: Microsoft plans to shut down To Do on June 30, 2027, moving work and school users to Planner but offering no direct replacement for personal accounts, GeekWire reports. Longtime users of the popular list app are pushing back.

markets.asOf: market close, Fri Nov 20 (futures reopen 5 PM CT Sunday); Bitcoin as of Sunday
markets.summary: Stocks are coming off Wall Street's worst week since April 2025, with the S&P 500 and Dow in correction; Bitcoin rebounded about 5% Sunday after hitting a two-year low Saturday.

other.headline: Iran says Bahrain strikes targeted US Patriot sites; tanker incidents reported
other.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Saturday's attack on Bahrain, which sparked a fire at an industrial site in Sitra and injured two people, was aimed at US Patriot missile sites; Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar condemned it. On Sunday the IRGC claimed it downed a US drone near the Strait of Hormuz, and UK maritime authorities reported an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman.

other.headline: Dymer strike death toll rises to four
other.summary: Zelensky said Sunday evening that four people were killed when a Russian drone tore apart a section of a five-story apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, and that there was still no word on about 10 others. Rescuers pulled a child alive from the rubble; a separate strike on a supermarket in Vyshneve killed three.

other.headline: NATO's eastern flank reports airspace scares
other.summary: Poland's operational commander said a NATO Gripen pilot was cleared to shoot down a suspected Russian cruise missile over Poland on Nov. 20 but couldn't identify it in bad weather. Moldova reported a Russian drone crossing its airspace twice, and Finland is probing a suspected helicopter incursion.
other.source: Kyiv Independent via Ukraine desk note

other.headline: Trump orders contractors to loop in White House on congressional requests
other.summary: President Trump signed an executive order directing federal contractors to coordinate with the White House when congressional committees ask them for information, a move that bears on Congress's direct oversight of companies doing government work.

other.headline: China's tech giants set to double AI spending
other.summary: Research firm Rhodium estimates China's largest tech companies will double capital spending to about $139 billion in 2026, while AI lab revenue covers less than 8% of that outlay, The New York Times reports.

other.headline: Verstappen wins chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix
other.summary: Max Verstappen won Saturday night's race on the Strip as Lando Norris passed Kimi Antonelli for second on the final lap. George Russell crashed out and the two Ferraris collided.
